title: data/publish/.../meta.json
description: Per-cell metadata for handball. Schema v2 is REQUIRED here, unlike football's: these cells are new and emit the full v2 contract from their first publish, whereas the live football tree predates it.

division.description: Division code from config/leagues.yml publish_divisions. The leading character may be a digit: basketball's second tier is coded 1D.

n_rounds.description: Rounds in the REGULAR season, derived upstream and published so a consumer never has to guess it. null on a cup. It is not 2*(n_teams-1): Icelandic women's handball plays a triple round robin (8 teams, 84 fixtures, 21 rounds).

n_rounds_source.description: Where n_rounds came from. `config` = the division's configured expected_meetings (wins); `schedule` = derived from the season's fixture count; `none` = neither was available; `not_applicable` = a cup, which has no round count.

units.description: The scale the published strength and home-advantage bands are on, and the goal-difference bin width the extractor binned with. The 2DT models are additive in raw points/goals; football's bivariate Poisson is on the log scale. Getting this wrong is a home edge of 4 points publishing as 54.6.

points.description: The league points scheme. `draw` is null where a draw is impossible (basketball), so no consumer infers one from a 0.

season_scope.description: Narrowed: the published table is the regular season and the post-season is not modelled, so placement 1 is top of the regular-season table and NOT the title.

postseason.description: Non-nullable here: both 2DT sports have an urslitakeppni this model does not simulate, and saying so is the whole point of the D3 relabel.

qualify.description: The configured qualification cut, or null where the division has none. Only football's Besta deild configures one today: no single per-division integer describes basketball's four different post-season structures, one of which takes every team through.

relegation.description: The configured relegation cut. `slots` is null where no division configures relegation_slots, which is everywhere today.
